1.name: James Gallagher
1.background: Attorney and partner in his family's farming operation who served in the California State Assembly from 2014 and was Assembly Republican leader from 2022 to 2025. He won the June 2, 2026 special election with 62.1 percent to fill the vacancy left by Doug LaMalfa's death and took office that month. He also advanced from the concurrent top-two primary for the full term, against Democrat Mike McGuire.
priorities: Lower the cost of living through lower taxes, fees and regulation
Expand energy production to bring prices down
Tougher crime laws and continued border security

cost.label: Runs on 'expand energy production to bring prices down' and making life affordable 'through lower taxes, lower fees and fewer regulations' (campaign site)

health.label: Mixed: 'I think we do need to restore the Medi-Cal funding, but not for illegal immigrants', while calling seismic mandates on rural hospitals 'crazy' and urging 'reasonable things to cut their costs' (NSPR interview)

housing.label: 'You're never going to get there unless you reduce the input costs that go into market housing'; 'you have to remove those barriers that get in the way of building the project' (Chico News and Review)

immigration.label: Campaign pledge to 'continue the tough border security implemented by the President' (campaign site)

taxes.label: Campaign pledge to 'make life more affordable for North State families through lower taxes, lower fees and fewer regulations' (campaign site)

climate.label: 'Expand energy production to bring prices down'; blames California policy for high gas prices (campaign site)

safety.label: Campaign pledge to 'enact tougher laws protect our communities, neighborhoods and homes from crime' (campaign site)

nullNotes.education: Checked the campaign site, which states no K-12 position, the Chico News and Review and NSPR primary interviews, and Ballotpedia, which records he filed no Candidate Connection survey in 2014, 2020, 2022 or 2024. His only education items are expanding community college vocational programs in nursing, logging and forestry, and a general parental rights line, neither of which maps onto the public investment versus school choice axis.
nullNotes.repro: Checked the campaign site, which states no abortion position, both 2026 primary interviews, Ballotpedia and Wikipedia. No abortion position is documented in this race.
nullNotes.democracy: Checked the campaign site, which states no elections position, both primary interviews and Ballotpedia. His only elections item is opposing partisan redistricting after Proposition 50, which is not a voting access or voter ID position and does not map onto this axis.

1.name: Mike McGuire
1.background: State senator for California's 2nd District since 2014 and president pro tempore of the State Senate from February 2024 until November 2025, the first North Coast senator to lead the chamber since 1866. He was elected to the Healdsburg School Board at 19 and later served on the city council and the Sonoma County Board of Supervisors. He advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary to face Republican James Gallagher in November.
priorities: Pass Medicare for All and keep rural hospitals open
Lower costs for working families and take on corporate price gouging
Wildfire protection and doubling the CalFire firefighting force

cost.label: 'Lowering Costs for Working Families' plank: 'I'll raise wages, take on corporate price gouging, and fight to bring down the cost of living' (campaign issues)

health.label: 'Healthcare can't just be for the wealthy few'; 'In Congress, I'll fight to pass Medicare for All and keep rural hospitals open' (campaign issues)

housing.label: 'Tackling the Cost of Housing' plank backs affordable housing investments and renter protections (campaign issues)

immigration.label: Runs a 'Holding ICE Accountable' plank opposing what he calls the weaponization of government against Americans: 'I won't back down from that fight' (campaign issues)

taxes.label: 'Making Billionaires Pay Their Fair Share' plank: 'Here in California, I've made billionaires pay their fare share' and 'I've taken on big corporations and won' (campaign issues)

climate.label: 'I've led the fight for stronger environmental laws and climate action, and taken on Big Oil'; 'Fighting for Climate Action' plank pledges wildfire prevention investment (campaign issues)

safety.label: As Senate leader fast-tracked the 2024 retail theft package, including retail crime restraining orders and cross-jurisdictional charging: they 'give prosecutors, judges and law enforcement the enhanced tools they need'; his remarks address no treatment or prevention element (California Senate)

repro.label: 'Women, not politicians, should make their own healthcare decisions'; 'I'll defend reproductive freedom, protect access to contraception and IVF, and make these rights the law of the land, once and for all' (campaign issues)

democracy.label: 'Defending Democracy and Our Rights' plank centers protecting voting rights and civil rights, with a separate plank to overturn Citizens United (campaign issues)

nullNotes.education: Read the full issues page, all twelve planks: education appears only inside 'Creating Good Jobs and Investing in Rural Communities' as job training and broadband. Also checked the NSPR primary interview, where his education items are community college career academies and college affordability, plus Ballotpedia and Wikipedia. Nothing maps onto the K-12 public investment versus school choice axis.

4.name: Mike Thompson
4.background: Vietnam veteran and Napa Valley vineyard manager who served in the California State Senate before winning his U.S. House seat in 1998, making this his fourteenth term. He is ranking member of the Ways and Means Subcommittee on Tax Policy and a member of the Blue Dog Coalition. He led the primary field on June 2, 2026 and faces fellow Democrat Eric Jones in November under California's top-two system.
priorities: Treat health care as a right and reverse the Medicaid cuts
Tax policy that does not cut rates for million dollar earners

health.label: 'I believe health care is a right. Congress must work to help everyone in America gain access to quality, affordable health care' (official House site)

housing.label: 'Lack of affordable housing is devastating California families'; works through Ways and Means and Appropriations on Low-Income Housing Tax Credits and federal assistance (official House site)

immigration.label: Voted no on the Laken Riley Act, which requires ICE detention for certain charged noncitizens, on passage January 7, 2025 (House roll call 6)

taxes.label: 'I'm of a strong belief that if you're making a million bucks a year, you don't need any tax help in this environment' (Davis Vanguard)

climate.label: 'I strongly support investing in land conservation, acting to prevent climate change and transitioning to a clean energy economy' (official House site)

education.label: 'Congress must invest in early childhood, special, technical and higher education programs' (official House site)

repro.label: Pro-choice despite being Roman Catholic; called the overturning of Roe v. Wade 'an assault on women' (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Voted no on the SAVE Act, which would require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, on passage April 10, 2025 (House roll call 102)

nullNotes.cost: Checked his official House issues page, which addresses the economy only as 'a good-paying job that helps them provide for their families', the August 2026 Davis Vanguard interview, where he says 'people are struggling' without naming a mechanism, and Wikipedia. No price, wage or subsidy position documented.
nullNotes.safety: Checked his official House issues page, which contains no crime content, the Davis Vanguard interview and Wikipedia. The only item is a 2015 proposal for tougher penalties on illegal marijuana growers on trespassed land, which is too narrow to place him on the prevention versus enforcement axis.

4.name: Eric Jones
4.background: First generation college graduate who attended Yale on a full scholarship and became a partner at the investment firm Dragoneer, with earlier work at companies including Lyra Health, Duolingo and Chime. He and his wife founded the Rachel and Eric Jones Foundation and the American Dream Institute. A political newcomer, he outraised the fourteen term incumbent and finished second in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, setting up an all Democratic November race against Mike Thompson.
priorities: A working class tax refund paid for by ending corporate tax dodging
Expand Medicare and lower prescription drug costs
End PG&E monopoly abuses and lower utility bills

cost.label: Platform is 'end PG&E's monopoly and lower your utility bills', a 'Working Class Refund & Tax Cut', 'lower prescription drug costs' through negotiation and 'make rent tax-deductible' (campaign site)

health.label: Backs Medicare for All along with expanded coverage for dental, vision and hearing care (KQED)

housing.label: Campaign themes 'Zero-Down Pathways to Homeownership' and 'Investing in Affordable Housing', backing 'major federal investments to build housing that workers, families, and seniors can afford' (Ballotpedia)

immigration.label: 'Tackling Immigration' theme calls for 'a humane, orderly, and fair immigration system that keeps families together, strengthens our economy, and restores accountability' (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: 'The core of my platform is forcing corporations to actually follow the tax code we have on the books, closing corporate loopholes, and using that money to fund a tax cut for the working class in this country' (KQED)

climate.label: Campaign themes include support for 'union jobs' and 'clean energy' investments (Ballotpedia)

nullNotes.education: Checked the campaign site platform list, the Ballotpedia profile, which records no 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and the KQED and Davis Vanguard race coverage. Education appears only as a general reference to restoring the American Dream through education access, with no position on public school funding or school choice.
nullNotes.safety: Checked the campaign site platform list, which has no crime plank, the Ballotpedia profile and the KQED and Davis Vanguard race coverage. No crime or policing position documented.
nullNotes.repro: Checked the campaign site platform list, the Ballotpedia profile and the KQED and Davis Vanguard race coverage. The closest item is 'expanding access to affordable women's health care' on his biography page, which does not state an abortion position.
nullNotes.democracy: Checked the campaign site platform list, the Ballotpedia profile and race coverage. His democracy items are 'ban members of Congress from trading stocks', '12-year term limits' and 'end gerrymandering, everywhere', none of which is a voting access or voter ID position and none of which maps onto this axis.

5.name: Tom McClintock
5.background: One of the longest serving fiscal conservatives in California politics, with more than two decades in the state legislature and a run for governor in the 2003 recall before winning his U.S. House seat in 2008. He sits on the Natural Resources, Judiciary and Budget committees and is a consistent vote against federal spending. He led the June 2, 2026 top-two primary and faces Democrat Michael Masuda in November.
priorities: Cut federal spending, subsidies, grants and earmarks
Open up resource and energy production
Repeal the Affordable Care Act and restore market competition in health care

cost.label: 'I continue to believe that the roots of all fiscal evil are subsidies, grants and earmarks'; argues subsidies 'force up prices for all' (official House site)

health.label: 'Price controls, which date back to Hammurabi's Code, consistently and unerringly produce a shortage of whatever commodity they're trying to control'; voted against drug price controls in H.R. 3 and for the American Health Care Act (official House site)

housing.label: 'The high cost of housing is the product of bad public policy that has imposed expensive mandates on construction, limited the permits that can be issued, restricted the land available for housing, and flooded the market with subsidies' (official House site)

immigration.label: Voted against the Fairness for High-Skilled Immigrants Act, against the appropriations increase in H-2B visas, and against barring ICE from acting on information about sponsors of unaccompanied children (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Voted yes on H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which made the 2017 tax cuts permanent, on July 3, 2025 (House roll call 190)

climate.label: Frames resource limits as the problem: 'the very things that make us prosperous and comfortable are the things the left attempts to put off limits'; spoke on the House floor for H.R. 3109, the REFINER Act (official House site)

education.label: On the elimination of the DC voucher program, 'what a pity it is to remove the only part of the nation's education system that actually works'; calls No Child Left Behind 'a disaster' (official House site)

safety.label: Mixed: authored California's lethal injection provision, but in 2020 was the sole House Republican to cosponsor the Ending Qualified Immunity Act (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Voted yes on H.R. 36, the Pain-Capable Unborn Child Protection Act, a 20-week abortion ban, May 13, 2015 (House roll call 223)

democracy.label: Voted yes on the SAVE Act, requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, April 10, 2025 (House roll call 102)

5.name: Michael Masuda
5.now: Electrical engineer, former U.S. State Department diplomat
5.background: Electrical engineer who spent seven years in defense research before serving three and a half years as a State Department diplomat working on science and technology policy. He grew up in Amador County and is the only Democrat in the race who lives inside the district. He advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary against sixteen year incumbent Tom McClintock, running on rural cost of living, wildfire and hospital access.
priorities: Lower housing, health care and energy costs in rural CA-5
Wildfire risk reduction and keeping home insurance available
Keep rural hospitals and clinics open

cost.label: Affordability plank targets 'major cost drivers: housing, healthcare, and energy', promises to 'reduce out-of-pocket expenses without shifting costs elsewhere' and to 'increase transparency where pricing is disconnected from real costs' (campaign issues)

health.label: Would 'protect Medicare and Medi-Cal', 'reduce prescription drug and out-of-pocket costs' and 'strengthen oversight to address cost drivers' (campaign issues)

housing.label: Mixed: would 'expand proven federal programs that finance affordable housing' and back prevention focused homelessness programs, while also promising to 'lower the cost of building' by streamlining federal delays (campaign issues)

immigration.label: Mixed: 'secure the border, enforce the law' and 'prioritize removal of individuals who pose public safety risks', alongside 'expand and modernize legal pathways' and 'provide an earned, lawful path forward' with 'certainty for Dreamers' (campaign issues)

taxes.label: Faults the incumbent for 'backing tax cuts that benefit corporations and the wealthy' while voting against rural hospital and wildfire funding (campaign issues)

education.label: Focus is 'strengthening public education': increase special education investment, 'reduce class sizes', address teacher shortages, and 'strengthen programs like Title I and IDEA' (campaign issues)

safety.label: Safety items are prevention side only: 'support prevention-focused approaches to student safety', expand school based mental health, and 'support treatment and recovery-focused programs' for addiction (campaign issues)

democracy.label: On election fraud, 'I firmly believe that it just does not exist at a level that is impacting our elections' (The Modesto Focus)

nullNotes.repro: Read the full issues page, all ten sections: there is no abortion plank, and the LGBTQ+ section's health line is about 'medically appropriate care' generally. Also checked the Turlock Journal profile and The Modesto Focus interview, neither of which raises abortion. No abortion position documented.

6.name: Kevin Kiley
6.background: Former high school teacher, deputy attorney general and California state legislator who ran in the 2021 recall election against Gavin Newsom before winning a House seat in 2022. He left the Republican Party in March 2026 and is running for reelection as an independent, which is why the FEC record carries no major party. He advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary against Democrat Richard Pan.
priorities: Roll back state mandates that raise the cost of living
Expand school choice through education tax credits
Limit state taxing power over former residents

health.label: Voted yes on H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, the law that cut Medicaid, on July 3, 2025 (House roll call 190)

housing.label: In his 2021 recall campaign: 'the cost of living in California, especially housing, which gets worse every year as a result of deliberate policy choices even as lawmakers claim they are addressing the problem' (Ballotpedia)

immigration.label: Voted yes on the Laken Riley Act, which requires ICE detention for certain charged noncitizens, on passage January 7, 2025 (House roll call 6)

taxes.label: Voted yes on H.R. 1, which made the 2017 tax cuts permanent, on July 3, 2025 (House roll call 190)

climate.label: Acknowledges climate change is real but opposes state mandates, having fought Newsom's order requiring zero emission vehicles by 2035 and the 2045 oil drilling ban, and moved to end federal funding for High-Speed Rail (Wikipedia)

education.label: Supports charter schools and school choice, criticized teachers' unions as overly powerful, and authored 2018 legislation making it easier for students to transfer school districts (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Voted yes on the SAVE Act, requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, April 10, 2025 (House roll call 102)

nullNotes.cost: Checked his official House site, which carries legislative news rather than issue pages, Wikipedia and Ballotpedia, which records no Candidate Connection survey in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2024 or 2026. His one cost of living statement is about housing specifically and is scored there rather than counted twice.
nullNotes.safety: Checked his official House site, Wikipedia and Ballotpedia. The nearest item is a 2021 proposal to audit homelessness spending, which is a spending accountability position rather than a policing or sentencing one.
nullNotes.repro: Checked his official House site, Wikipedia and Ballotpedia, which records no Candidate Connection survey for any year. Advocacy group scorecards exist but the run book bars citing an aggregator in place of the underlying vote, and no underlying abortion vote of his was located.

6.name: Richard Pan
6.now: Pediatrician and professor at UC Davis
6.background: Pediatrician and UC Davis professor who led the university's pediatric residency program before serving in the California Assembly and State Senate from 2010 to 2022. He is best known for Senate Bill 277, the 2015 law that ended personal belief exemptions to school vaccine requirements after a measles outbreak. He says the dismantling of federal public health work under RFK Jr. is what pushed him to run, and he advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary against Kevin Kiley.
priorities: Stop the gutting of the Affordable Care Act and protect Medicare
Lower prescription drug and health care costs
Restore science and public health to federal policy

cost.label: Says he 'passed laws that cut the price of insulin' and pledges to keep fighting to lower prescription drug and health care costs (campaign site)

health.label: Would 'stop Trump from gutting the Affordable Care Act, protect Medicare' and 'stop insurance companies from denying critical care prescribed by doctors' (campaign site)

housing.label: 'Passed legislation to help families with housing costs' (campaign site)

immigration.label: Will 'fight for a path to citizenship' and would overhaul ICE so it enforces the law fairly and protects constitutional rights (campaign site)

safety.label: Would 'invest in first responders, mental health grants, and community-based violence prevention programs that stop crime before people are hurt' (campaign site)

repro.label: Would 'work to codify Roe' and has ensured coverage for abortion access and contraception (campaign site)

democracy.label: Faults Kiley as 'unwilling to truly challenge the president when he commits things like trying to challenge a free and fair election', and says 'our constitution counts on us, the people and our elected leaders, to actually look out for it' (campaign release)

nullNotes.taxes: Checked the campaign site, which has no tax plank, the general election kickoff release, Ballotpedia, which records no Candidate Connection survey, and Wikipedia. The only tax item in the race is Kiley's charge that Pan cast the deciding vote for the state gas tax, which is an opponent's claim and a fuel levy rather than a position on corporate or high earner rates.
nullNotes.climate: Checked the campaign site, whose only environment line is to 'fight for facts and science to guide federal policy on the environment', the kickoff release, Ballotpedia and Wikipedia. Nothing states a direction on clean energy transition versus expanded production.
nullNotes.education: Checked the campaign site, the kickoff release, Ballotpedia and Wikipedia. His education items are 'loan relief for educational debt' and workforce training and apprenticeships, which do not map onto the public school investment versus school choice axis.

7.name: Doris Matsui
7.background: Born in the Poston internment camp in Arizona and raised in Dinuba, she worked in the Clinton White House before winning the Sacramento seat in a 2005 special election following the death of her husband, Congressman Robert Matsui. She is a senior member of the Energy and Commerce Committee and worked on passage of the Affordable Care Act. She faces fellow Democrat Mai Vang in November after the June 2, 2026 top-two primary.
priorities: Defend and build on the Affordable Care Act
Make Sacramento a clean energy hub and reach 100 percent clean energy by 2030
Universal access to quality education from pre-K through college

cost.label: Campaign credits her with helping 'lower prescription drug prices' from the Energy and Commerce Committee (campaign site)

health.label: 'At its core, the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act is about providing affordable access to high quality health coverage for all Americans'; led creation of the ACA's Prevention and Public Health Fund (official House site)

immigration.label: Voted no on the Laken Riley Act, which requires ICE detention for certain charged noncitizens, on passage January 7, 2025 (House roll call 6)

taxes.label: Favors progressive taxation and closing offshore business loopholes, and opposed extending capital gains and dividend tax breaks (Wikipedia)

climate.label: Works to 'bring clean energy technology to Sacramento' and backs 'clean school buses and 100% clean energy by 2030' (official House site)

education.label: 'Universal access to quality education is one of Congresswoman Matsui's top priorities'; works with local school districts on federal grants and supports the Pell Grant program against cuts (official House site)

repro.label: Called the Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade 'devastating' and said she was 'deeply heartbroken and angered' by it (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Voted no on the SAVE Act, which would require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, April 10, 2025 (House roll call 102)

nullNotes.housing: Checked her official House issues index, which lists health care, clean energy and climate, education and economy and jobs but no housing page, her campaign site, and Wikipedia, which states nothing on housing. No housing position documented.
nullNotes.safety: Checked her official House issues index, which has no crime page, her campaign site and Wikipedia. Her only public safety material is gun regulation, including ammunition purchase limits and the gun show loophole, and the run book excludes gun stances from this axis.

7.name: Mai Vang
7.background: Daughter of Hmong refugees, born in Sacramento, who served on the Sacramento City Unified School Board before winning a city council seat in 2020, and who lectures in ethnic studies at Sacramento State. On the council she created the city's first Children's Fund and secured its first citywide language access coordinator. She says increased ICE activity in the region is what pushed her to run, and she would be the first Hmong American in Congress.
priorities: Medicare for All to guarantee healthcare as a right
Abolish ICE and create a comprehensive pathway to citizenship
Take on corporate landlords and build a Federal Renters' Bill of Rights

cost.label: Platform is to break up monopolies, take on price gouging, raise the minimum wage tied to inflation, and guarantee paid family leave and sick days (campaign platform)

health.label: Commits to 'Medicare for All to guarantee healthcare as a right', plus eliminating medical debt and cutting prescription costs (campaign platform)

housing.label: Would massively increase federal construction funding, bar corporations from buying single family homes, and establish a 'Federal Renters' Bill of Rights' with eviction protections (campaign platform)

immigration.label: Platform centers abolishing ICE, defunding deportation machinery and closing for-profit detention, alongside 'a comprehensive pathway to citizenship' (campaign platform)

taxes.label: 'I'll vote to make billionaires pay their fair share and close corporate loopholes so we can invest that money back into the communities that need it' (campaign platform)

climate.label: Backs transitioning to clean energy with 'good-paying jobs', holding polluters accountable, and directing 'at least 40% of federal climate dollars to communities most impacted by pollution' (campaign platform)

education.label: 'I'll fight to protect their funding and resist efforts to divert public dollars to charter schools or private voucher programs'; also backs free public college tuition (campaign platform)

safety.label: Opposes police militarization in schools and backs restorative justice; was the sole council vote against renewing ShotSpotter gunshot detection, citing false positive rates (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Treats 'reproductive care as healthcare' and would codify abortion rights federally and oppose contraception restrictions (campaign platform)

democracy.label: Platform is to protect voting rights and reverse Citizens United by constitutional amendment; she has organized for 'Vote 16' initiatives to extend the franchise to sixteen year olds (campaign platform)

8.name: John Garamendi
8.background: Raised on a cattle ranch in Mokelumne Hill, he served in the California legislature, as the state's first elected insurance commissioner, as deputy interior secretary under President Clinton and as lieutenant governor before winning a House seat in a 2009 special election. He works on maritime, agriculture and armed services issues. He advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary against Republican Rudy Recile.
priorities: Good-paying jobs and closing the gap between the wealthy and working families
Increase funding for federal housing and homelessness programs
Criminal justice reform that addresses systemic bias

cost.label: 'My top priorities in Congress are creating good-paying jobs for Americans and combating the growing gap between the wealthy and working families'; 'I was proud to vote in support of the Inflation Reduction Act' (official House site)

health.label: Cosponsored the Medicare for All Act of 2021 (Wikipedia)

housing.label: 'I consistently advocate to increase funding for federal housing programs and ensure no American is priced out of a home'; secured low income housing construction money and backs Homeless Assistance Program funding (official House site)

immigration.label: Voted no on the Laken Riley Act, which requires ICE detention for certain charged noncitizens, on passage January 7, 2025 (House roll call 6)

taxes.label: Called the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act a 'tax scam' benefiting the wealthy and corporations rather than middle class Americans (Wikipedia)

climate.label: Backed the Green New Deal: 'I welcome the energy and commitment of the supporters of H.Res.109, and I join with them as I continue my decades-long effort to stop Climate Change' (Wikipedia)

education.label: 'I have consistently spoken out against the destructive cuts to all levels of education and am a fierce advocate for both students and teachers'; page states no support for vouchers or choice (official House site)

safety.label: Original cosponsor of the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act; frames safety around eliminating 'systemic bias and racism' and says safety 'cannot be advanced without practical criminal justice reforms that foster equity' (official House site)

repro.label: Called Roe v. Wade a 'fundamental human right to bodily autonomy' and called the 2022 decision overturning it 'devastating' (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Voted no on the SAVE Act, which would require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, April 10, 2025 (House roll call 102)

9.name: Josh Harder

He is one of the House Democrats who most often breaks with his party, including a vote for the Laken Riley Act and a public safety agenda built on police hiring grants. He advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary against Republican John McBride.
priorities: Bring down prices on housing, utilities, gas and groceries
Treat health care as a right and stop Medicaid cuts
Restore federal law enforcement hiring grants

cost.label: 'Prices are skyrocketing, from housing and utilities to gas and groceries'; capped the price of insulin at $35 a month and leads the fight to stop PG&E rate increases, while also calling to suspend the gas tax (official House site)

health.label: 'Health care is a right, plain and simple'; runs on protecting the Affordable Care Act, expanding coverage and condemning cuts to Medicaid (official House site)

immigration.label: Mixed: 'a comprehensive, humane, and bipartisan immigration system that allows people to get right with the law and come out of the shadows', alongside 'keeping our border secure' and '21st century investments in border security' (official House site)

taxes.label: Voted no on H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which made the 2017 tax cuts permanent, on July 3, 2025 (House roll call 190)

safety.label: Would 'restore federal funding for law enforcement hiring grants to their original level', funded a Stockton PD Real Time Crime Center, and pushes targeted prosecution of mail theft and cybercrime; the page names no root cause measures (official House site)

repro.label: Supports legal abortion rights (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Voted no on the SAVE Act, which would require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, April 10, 2025 (House roll call 102)

9.name: John McBride
9.background: Strength and conditioning coach who came to California in 1989 and spent 12 years as strength and conditioning coach at the University of the Pacific and 13 years at St. Mary's High School, mentoring athletes in the San Joaquin area. He grew up in Meriden, Connecticut, and describes himself as a man of faith. He completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey in 2024 and advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary against Josh Harder.
priorities: Reduce taxes and drastically shrink government spending

health.label: Health platform is 'medical freedom', 'greater emphasis on natural healing methods' and 'no death boards', with no expansion of public coverage (campaign site)

immigration.label: 'Our borders must be protected at all costs the invasion being allowed at our southern border will destroy this nation' (Ballotpedia Candidate Connection)

taxes.label: Economy platform is 'reduce oppressive tax policies', 'drastically shrink government spending' and 'no tax on Social Security' (campaign site)

climate.label: 'Energy independence must be restored. America has the largest natural resources in the world for us to achieve energy independence and it is not being used' (Ballotpedia Candidate Connection)

safety.label: Mixed: his Safer Communities list runs 'support for local law enforcement' and 'support criminal prosecution' alongside 'mental health initiatives' and 'support for youth and families' (campaign site)

nullNotes.cost: Checked the campaign site, whose economy list is entirely tax, spending, small business and energy items, and his 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. Neither names prices, inflation or wages, so his tax and spending positions are scored on the taxes axis and not counted again here.
nullNotes.housing: Checked the campaign site, which lists homelessness under a youth heading but no housing policy, and his 2024 Candidate Connection survey. No housing supply, zoning or renter position documented.
nullNotes.repro: Checked the campaign site, which has no abortion item, and his 2024 Candidate Connection survey, whose closest line is a general Bill of Rights statement. No abortion position documented.
nullNotes.democracy: Checked the campaign site, whose Liberty list contains the bare phrase 'Voting Rights' with no direction, plus 'no CBDC', and his 2024 Candidate Connection survey. Nothing states a position on voting access or voter identification.

10.name: Mark Desaulnier
10.background: Former restaurant owner who served as a Concord city councilman and mayor, a Contra Costa County supervisor, and a member of both houses of the California legislature before winning his House seat in 2014. He sits on the Education and Workforce and Transportation committees and sponsors the Medicare for All Act. He advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary against Republican Jeff Frese.
priorities: Protect, strengthen and expand the Affordable Care Act
Expand housing and affordable options in the Bay Area
Restore the balance of power in favor of the American worker

cost.label: 'Restoring the balance of power in favor of the American worker is imperative'; cites that since 1979 wages rose 14.8 percent while productivity rose more than 64 percent (official House site)

health.label: 'Ardent supporter of protecting, strengthening, and expanding the Affordable Care Act' and a sponsor of the Medicare for All Act; wants a system 'that prioritizes people over profits' (official House site)

housing.label: 'The need to expand housing and provide more affordable options in the San Francisco Bay Area could not be more urgent'; authored the Housing Innovation Act and loans for affordable transit oriented housing, and urged eviction protections (official House site)

immigration.label: Voted no on the Laken Riley Act, which requires ICE detention for certain charged noncitizens, on passage January 7, 2025 (House roll call 6)

taxes.label: Voted no on H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which made the 2017 tax cuts permanent, on July 3, 2025 (House roll call 190)

climate.label: 'Recognizes climate change for the existential threat that it is' and champions policies that reduce greenhouse gas emissions (official House site)

education.label: 'Values a public education, programs to support the whole child, accessible and affordable college opportunities'; the page states no support for vouchers or choice (official House site)

repro.label: 'Strong supporter of the Women's Health Protection Act, which blocks medically unnecessary abortion restrictions'; sponsors the Right to Contraception Act and the Access to Family Building Act (official House site)

democracy.label: Voted no on the SAVE Act, which would require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, April 10, 2025 (House roll call 102)

nullNotes.safety: Checked his official House issues index, whose only public safety page is Gun Violence Prevention, plus Wikipedia, where the criminal justice material is a state bill requiring gun owners to report stolen weapons. 10.background: Small business owner and father from Contra Costa County who has no FEC candidate record and ran a locally focused campaign, arguing his opponent is preoccupied with national and international matters. Cut red tape that makes building slow and expensive
Back the police and get fentanyl off the streets

cost.label: 'Stop the deficit spending that drives up mortgage rates and prices' (campaign site)

housing.label: Mixed: 40,000 attainable homes via faster permitting and lower fees AND down-payment help plus a ban on algorithmic rent collusion by corporate landlords (campaign site)

taxes.label: Mixed: keep TABOR's voter-approval requirement for tax increases; open to revenue changes for childcare (Colorado Sun issue guide)

climate.label: Meet emission-reduction goals: Geothermal Development Authority, battery storage, EV incentives, heat-pump rates (campaign site)

education.label: Livable teacher wages plus teacher housing aid; defend public schools against privatization; expand Universal Preschool (campaign site)

safety.label: Mixed: police recruitment and modernized training AND co-responder mental-health teams, risk-based bail (campaign site)

repro.label: Defend reproductive rights 'including Amendment 79 and against any attacks on our laws protecting the right to choose' (campaign site)

democracy.label: 'Defend Colorado's gold-standard voting laws against political power plays and retaliation' (campaign site)

governor.name: Victor Marx
governor.background: Founder of a religious humanitarian nonprofit and Marine Corps veteran; a political newcomer who describes himself as a 'high-risk humanitarian.' cost.label: Mixed-market: expand earned-income tax credits and preserve the senior homestead exemption while deregulating home building; audit every executive agency (campaign policies)

housing.label: Expedited permitting with statutory decision deadlines for home building; identify and roll back building, environmental, and energy mandates that raise construction costs (campaign policies)

immigration.label: End sanctuary policies, require cooperation with federal authorities, Border-Related Crime Strike Force (campaign policies)

taxes.label: Phased income-tax rate reduction when verified surpluses exist, veto new fees that act as de facto taxes, enforce TABOR limits (campaign policies)

climate.label: 'All-of-the-above' energy strategy expanding renewables 'while maintaining the vital role of oil, gas, hydroelectric power' (campaign policies)

education.label: Expand school choice via education savings accounts; parental curriculum access (campaign policies)

safety.label: End catch-and-release for violent offenders, deny bail for violent felonies, make fentanyl a statewide emergency priority (campaign policies)

democracy.label: Voter ID for all ballots, annual voter-roll maintenance, ballot chain-of-custody standards (campaign policies)

controversies.label: Ministry stories are largely unverifiable, including saying his stepfather forced him to kill a man at age 7; sidestepped debates and forums; rivals Kirkmeyer ('a disaster for our state') and Bottoms ('con man') said they would not support him (Colorado Sun)

at-large.name: Julie Fedorchak

sources.label: House roll call 114, 2025, California Clean Cars waiver disapproval

at-large.now: U.S. House of Representatives (North Dakota at-large)
at-large.background: Freshman U.S. Representative for North Dakota's at-large district since January 2025 and a member of the moderate Republican Governance Group. She spent twelve years on the North Dakota Public Service Commission, from 2013 to 2025, regulating utilities and pipelines, and campaigns on that record. She has introduced legislation to eliminate the Inflation Reduction Act's wind and solar tax credits for new projects, arguing intermittent generation poses reliability risks to the grid. She was renominated in the June 9, 2026 primary over Alex Balazs.
priorities: Unleash domestic energy and agriculture production
Cut federal spending and balance the budget

cost.label: Campaign priorities are to 'Curb Inflation That Is Crushing Families', 'Rein in Overreaching Federal Agencies', 'Stop out of Control Spending and Balance the Budget' and 'Unleash America's Energy and Agriculture Industries', with a record of 'Cutting Regulatory Red Tape' and 'Fighting Against Over-Regulation of the Coal Industry' (campaign site)

health.label: Calls the Affordable Care Act the 'Unaffordable Care Act' and says 'Obamacare is anything but affordable'; voted against the Democrat-led discharge petition to extend the enhanced premium tax credits; wants Medicaid 'reforms' that 'restore the program to its original mission'; health decisions belong with 'doctors and patients in North Dakota, not in Washington, D.C.' (House office issues page)

immigration.label: 'It was something I campaigned on. I would give us an A on our work so far. We have basically shut the border down' (North Dakota Monitor candidate issue spotlight)

taxes.label: Voted Aye on H.R. 1, titled 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act' on the roll call, on the motion to concur in the Senate amendment, July 3, 2025; it passed 218 to 214 (House roll call 190)

climate.label: Voted Yea on H.J.Res.88, titled on the roll call as congressional disapproval of the EPA rule on 'California State Motor Vehicle and Engine Pollution Control Standards; Advanced Clean Cars II; Waiver of Preemption', May 1, 2025; it passed 246 to 164 (House roll call 114)

repro.label: 'As a Christian, wife, and mother, I believe in the sanctity of life and am committed to protecting the unborn'; the page carries 'Fedorchak Votes to Pass Two Pro-Life Bills', January 23, 2026 (House office issues page)

democracy.label: Voted for the SAVE Act's voter identification requirement, saying it would 'improve election integrity in the U.S. and restore faith many people have lost in the election process', and says 'the federal government has a role to play in ensuring that American citizens are voting in American elections' (North Dakota Monitor candidate issue spotlight)

safety.label: Voted Aye on H.R. 6260, the Keeping Violent Offenders Off Our Streets Act, May 14, 2026, which passed 243 to 179 (House roll call 169)

education.label: Voted Aye on H.R. 2616, titled 'PROTECT Kids Act' on the roll call, a parental notification measure, May 20, 2026; it passed 217 to 198 (House roll call 184)

nullNotes.housing: checked her campaign site and its subpages, all eight fetchable House office issue pages including Budget and Economy, three pages of her House press release index, her Ballotpedia profile where she has completed no Candidate Connection survey, and North Dakota Monitor race coverage; no position on housing supply, zoning, permitting, or renters documented

at-large.name: Trygve Hammer
at-large.now: Freight rail conductor, former public school science teacher
at-large.background: Naval Academy graduate and former Marine helicopter pilot who served a combat deployment in Iraq, with later service as forward air controller and military attache at the U.S. Embassy in Rome. He has worked in the Bakken oil fields, taught seventh through twelfth grade science in North Dakota, and worked as a freight rail conductor. He took about 30 percent against Fedorchak in 2024 and was endorsed by the Democratic-NPL convention in March 2026 for a rematch. His stated frame is congressional oversight: 'If our federal delegation would act as a check on the worst impulses of the Trump administration, they would make it a better presidency.'
priorities: Tax fairness so corporations and the ultra wealthy pay more
Defending Social Security and rural healthcare access

cost.label: Mixed: 'Raising reference prices will be an important part of the new farm bill' and names processor concentration, 'Four of them control 85% of meat processing in this country', while also saying farmers and ranchers 'want to be out there and compete in the free market' and 'don't want to be propped up by the government' (North Dakota Monitor candidate interview, 2024)

taxes.label: Would 'remove the taxable income cap for Social Security', then $168,600, to increase the fund, and opposes raising the retirement age; his campaign priorities add that 'Profitable corporations and the ultra wealthy need to be paying their fair share' (North Dakota Monitor candidate interview, 2024)

immigration.label: Mixed: 'They are all human beings, and I have no problem with enforcement as long as it treats everybody like a human being', while insisting 'In the Constitution, the due process is to all persons, not to all citizens' and that judicial warrants be required to enter homes (North Dakota Monitor candidate issue spotlight)

climate.label: Mixed: says he is 'pro-American oil' and that record U.S. oil production 'should continue', while backing 'smaller, next generation nuclear technologies' as 'a carbon-free solution' with waste storage still an issue (North Dakota Monitor candidate interview, 2024)

education.label: 'We need support for, rather than attacks on, the public schools that are the source of pride' (campaign priorities page)

repro.label: Plank titled 'Protect women's freedom to make their own healthcare decisions': 'As long as we do not have full say on our personal medical decision, we do not have full liberty. The government should not intrude into our personal decisions as patients' (campaign priorities page)

democracy.label: Opposes the SAVE Act, 'The idea is to get people unregistered and to have fewer people vote', and on mail voting says 'It's secure here, and it's secure everywhere. I think it's leadership malpractice to be casting all this doubt on the electoral system' (North Dakota Monitor candidate issue spotlight)

health.label: Calls for mandatory rather than discretionary appropriations for the Indian Health Service 'to ensure stable and sufficient funding', and backs Tribal control of programs like SNAP; his documented health financing commitment is specific to Indian Country (campaign policies page)

nullNotes.housing: his tribal policies page backs 'full implementation' of the Tribal HUD-VASH Act for Native veterans, which is a veterans benefit rather than a general housing supply or renter position, so it does not score here; checked every page on his campaign site via its sitemap including /priorities, /policies, /about and 14 news items, his Ballotpedia profile with no completed Candidate Connection survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026, his iVoterGuide profile, and North Dakota Monitor coverage
nullNotes.safety: his Human Decency plank is about oversight of 'those in positions to protect and serve' and his tribal policies page covers Tribal criminal jurisdiction and an MMIP alert system, which are jurisdiction and victim notification questions rather than the prevention versus enforcement axis; no policing funding, sentencing, treatment, or reentry position found on any page of his campaign site, his Ballotpedia profile, his iVoterGuide profile which he left unanswered, or North Dakota Monitor coverage

at-large.name: Helene Neville
at-large.now: Registered nurse and public health educator
at-large.background: Registered nurse with 41 years of experience, including travel nursing, and a stage four Non-Hodgkin lymphoma survivor in remission. She ran across all 50 states, Puerto Rico, and parts of Mexico and Canada, close to 17,000 miles, to promote healthy living, and worked as a public health educator and liaison on federal Gulf War illness grants. She moved to North Dakota in 2020 and previously lived in Iowa. She entered the race seeking the Democratic-NPL nomination in February 2026 and is on the November ballot as an independent.
priorities: Healthcare and mental health access, especially rural
Cost of living, wages, and housing affordability

cost.label: 'End starvation wages. Raise & index the minimum wage. Protect full-time workers who still struggle', framed against 'Wages have not kept pace with rising costs' (campaign issues page)

health.label: 'Protecting Medicare and Medicaid means protecting the health and dignity of millions of Americans'; opposes 'significant cuts to Medicaid funding over the next decade and policies that could make it harder for millions of Americans to keep their coverage' (campaign Medicare and Medicaid page)

immigration.label: Backs 'Expanding lawful immigration pathways for workers and families', 'Providing stability for individuals brought to the United States as children through programs like DACA', and 'Maintaining a humane refugee and asylum system'; no enforcement first content on the page (campaign immigration page)

taxes.label: Mixed: platform calls to 'Tax corporate gains' and separately for 'no inheritance tax' (campaign issues page)

climate.label: Mixed: 'Support responsible energy development' and 'Energy independence, environmental stewardship, and economic growth can go hand in hand', with no emissions target or fuel source named (campaign climate and energy page)

education.label: 'To attract and retain the best teachers, we must ensure they are paid fairly'; notes North Dakota ranks 40th for teacher salaries and backs 'Investments in education for disadvantaged students and students with disabilities' and 'Strong funding for teacher professional development'; no voucher or charter content on the page (campaign education page)

safety.label: 'Addiction is not a moral failure, it is a medical condition'; would expand medication assisted treatment, mental health services and 'Prevention and early intervention programs', and hold pharmaceutical companies accountable; no policing or sentencing content on the page (campaign substance use page)

repro.label: 'I advocate for protecting reproductive freedom and ensuring people have the right to make choices about their own bodies and healthcare'; 'The government should not stand between a patient and their doctor' (campaign reproductive freedom page)

democracy.label: Mixed: 'Every eligible voter should be able to vote, every lawful vote should be counted', with 'Accessible voting for rural communities, seniors, veterans, and individuals with disabilities', alongside 'reasonable measures that verify voter eligibility' and 'Strong election security measures' (campaign issues page)

housing.label: Mixed: 'Policies should focus on expanding housing supply, encouraging responsible development, and ensuring that housing programs actually help families achieve stability', with the caution that 'when assistance increases, but housing supply does not, rents often rise alongside it' (campaign housing page)

senate.name: Cory Booker
senate.background: U.S. Senator since 2013 and former Mayor of Newark; ran for president in 2020. In 2025 he delivered the longest speech in Senate history (25 hours 5 minutes). Former tenants' rights lawyer.
priorities: Economic justice: baby bonds, EITC and child tax credit

cost.label: Targets 'the soaring cost of rent and predatory practices like overdraft fees'; championed EITC/child tax credit expansion (Senate issues)

health.label: Calls health care a fundamental human right; leader in protecting and building on the ACA (Senate issues)

housing.label: Made rental affordability a priority, 'cracking down on the soaring cost of rent' (Senate issues)

immigration.label: Backs protections for undocumented spouses and DACA recipients; urges comprehensive reform (Senate release)

taxes.label: Keep Your Pay Act: raise the corporate rate and make 'the wealthiest few and the biggest corporations' pay 'their fair share' to fund tax-free income up to $75,000 (Senate release)

climate.label: Original Green New Deal cosponsor; frames climate as an equity issue; lead on plastics reduction (Senate issues)

education.label: RAISE Act for up to $15,000 in teacher-pay tax credits; 'a student's zip code should not determine' their trajectory (Senate issues)

safety.label: Authored the First Step Act; works to end mass incarceration, reform sentencing, improve reentry (Senate issues)

repro.label: Introduced legislation affirming FDA preemption to protect medication-abortion access nationwide (Senate issues)

democracy.label: Co-led the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act: 'the right to vote is sacred for all Americans' (Senate release)

governor.name: Joe Lombardo
governor.background: Governor since 2023 after 34 years in law enforcement, including two terms as Clark County Sheriff (2015-2023). Army and Nevada National Guard veteran with UNLV degrees in civil engineering and crisis management. Won the June 9 Republican primary with 91% against six challengers.
priorities: No new taxes and lighter regulation

cost.label: On inflation: 'I can't control that', calls fix-it promises false; points instead to cutting employer taxes and eliminating over 900 regulations (Nevada Current)

health.label: Vetoed prescription drug price caps along with paid family leave and free school meals in a record 87-veto session (Nevada Current)

housing.label: Mixed: created a $250M state attainable-housing fund projected to leverage five times that in projects, paired with expedited permitting and prevailing-wage exemptions Democrats criticized (Nevada Independent)

immigration.label: Opposes sanctuary cities; as sheriff worked with ICE to identify and deport 'violent criminals' (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: Pledged to 'veto any new tax increase'; touts reduced employer taxes (Ballotpedia)

climate.label: Withdrew Nevada from the U.S. Climate Alliance, saying its goals 'conflict with Nevada's energy policy objectives'; ordered a 'balanced approach' pairing natural gas with renewables (Nevada Independent)

education.label: Supports expanding charter schools, 'school choice, and opportunity scholarships' plus read-by-three accountability (Ballotpedia)

safety.label: Opposes defunding police; pledges to 'put bad guys away' and keep communities safe (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: Mixed: self-described pro-life and endorsed by National Right to Life, but signed SB 131 shielding abortion patients and providers and says he will respect Nevada's voter-approved 24-week law (CBS News)

democracy.label: Proposed to 'eliminate ballot harvesting, end universal mail ballots, require an ID to vote' (Ballotpedia)

controversies.label: Settled a four-year Nevada Ethics Commission case over campaigning in his sheriff's uniform and badge, paying $5,000 with no willful violation found after the commission's original $20,000 fine and censure were challenged in court (Nevada Independent)

governor.background: Nevada Attorney General since 2019 and the first Black official elected to statewide constitutional office in Nevada; previously state Senate Majority Leader (2017-2019). Won the June 9 Democratic primary with 65% over Alexis Hill.
priorities: 'Affordable Nevada' agenda: housing, healthcare, and energy costs

health.label: Targets predatory pharmacy benefit managers and fraudulent medical billing; won more than $1.2B in opioid settlements as AG (campaign site)

climate.label: Backs 'clean and affordable energy', rooftop solar and efficiency incentives, and making data centers 'pay their fair share' for energy and water demands (campaign site)

education.label: Former math teacher who sued the Trump administration over dismantling the Department of Education to protect $1B in annual federal school funding (campaign site)

safety.label: Mixed 'tough and smart on crime': funds diversion courts and mental health programs while also 'increasing penalties for criminals who attack our law enforcement officers' (Ballotpedia)

democracy.label: Sued to block the Trump election order targeting mail ballots, defending Nevada's mail voting system (Nevada Current)

controversies.label: A 2026 ethics complaint over sponsored trips valued above $35,000 and campaign use of official social media advanced past initial review; IRS liens of $185,000 for 2010-2013 taxes were cleared in 2016 (Wikipedia)

2.now: Chair of the Town of Babylon Planning Board
2.background: Patrick Halpin is a Democrat who was the youngest person ever elected Suffolk County Executive, serving from 1988 to 1991. He was first elected to public office at age 26, to the Suffolk County Legislature from LD-13, and was the first Democrat in more than a century to win a New York State Assembly seat representing the Town of Babylon. He later chaired the Suffolk County Water Authority and the Town of Babylon Industrial Development Agency, and now chairs the Town of Babylon Planning Board. He launched this campaign for NY-02 through the committee Halpin for Congress and is the only Democrat listed for the June 23, 2026 primary.
priorities: the affordability crisis, from rent to childcare to medical bills
housing that keeps young people and workers on Long Island
protecting Long Island's drinking water aquifer

He was elected the first African American Justice of the Peace for Jefferson County Precinct 8 in 1994, taught American Government and Street Law at Memorial High School, pastored First Sixth Street Baptist Church, and works as a licensed funeral director and embalmer at Hannah Funeral Home. He holds a political science degree from Lamar University, a mortuary science certification, and a Master of Ministry from Tennessee Temple University Baptist Seminary. He reached the November ballot by winning the Democratic runoff over Richard Davis by roughly 200 votes following the March 3, 2026 primary.

16.background: Veronica Escobar has represented Texas' 16th Congressional District, entirely inside El Paso County, since January 2019. Before Congress she served as El Paso County Commissioner from 2006 to 2010 and as El Paso County Judge from 2011 to 2017, and she taught and worked in the nonprofit sector after earning a bachelor's degree from the University of Texas and a master's in English literature from New York University. She was one of the first two Latinas elected to Congress from Texas. She filed for re-election in 2026 and advanced through the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary to the November general election.

cost of living and wages for working families

38.background: Melissa A McDonough was born in Marietta, Ohio and has lived in Tomball, Texas for about 30 years.
